question: The Redhill cycling club stored 215 water bottles at its north depot, and a sponsor delivered 66 more to that same depot. The club keeps 2 depots in total, and the south depot holds exactly the same number of bottles as the north one. The club has been running for 38 years. At the spring race 91 bottles were handed out to riders. A charity later collected 242 bottles from the club. How many bottles does the club still have?

A gardener started with 121 seeds. They doubled the batch (multiplied by 2). They added 18 more seeds. They multiplied by 7 for harvest projection. They subtracted 428 seeds used in planting. The plot size was 200 square feet but didn't affect seed count. After doubling and adding but before the larger multiplication, how many seeds?

A bakery signed a contract to deliver bread to a hotel for 134 weeks. The hotel cancelled 43 of those weeks, then later extended the contract by 6 weeks. The bakery's scheduler counts in days rather than weeks, and since a week has 7 days, she wrote the contract length down in days. Each delivery van carries 500 loaves. So far 648 delivery days have been completed, 28 delivery days fall on public holidays with no delivery, and 2 days were lost to a snowstorm. How many delivery days remain?

In the morning Sam arrived at the arcade with 101 dollars, more than his friend Ivy had brought. He found 6 dollars on the floor and added them to his wallet. At the counter he exchanged every dollar he had for 2 tokens each. In the afternoon he spent 82 tokens on racing games and won 5 tokens back from a claw machine. In the evening the arcade ran a happy hour: a bonus machine paid out 8 tokens for every token fed into it, and Sam fed in all of his tokens and kept the payout. Ivy ended the day with fewer tokens than Sam. How many tokens did Sam have at the end of the evening?
A team had 109 points. Lost 57. Doubled afternoon. Multiplied by 9 tournament. Added 57 more. Converting to rounds, what is score?

A student had 118 dollars. They removed 113 dollars for textbooks. They multiplied by 9 to calculate semester budget. They added 48 dollars from part-time work. They removed 92 dollars for supplies. There was a 25-dollar grant (not used). How much was the semester budget?

A school starts the semester with 151 chairs in the auditorium, in a building that has hosted assemblies for a dozen decades, unrelated to today's count. A donation adds 10 more chairs. A second donation adds 73 more chairs. The chairs are then split evenly among 6 classrooms, and only one classroom's share is tracked. Finally, 29 chairs are removed from that classroom for repair. How many chairs does that classroom have now?
A farm had 102 animals. They added 16 animals. They removed 87 animals. They multiplied by 7 times. They added 56 animals. They multiplied by 7 times. Someone had a dozen animals. How many animals?

A single grain elevator started the day with 135 bushels of wheat. A local co-op delivery left the elevator with 9 times as much wheat. A regional contract then multiplied that amount by 5. A rail shipment of 1875 bushels was sent out to a mill, after a loading process that took about 60 minutes, exactly 1 hour. A final harvest bonus multiplied the remaining wheat by 5 once more. Finally, 30 more bushels arrived from a late delivery. How many bushels of wheat were left in the elevator?

A chocolate workshop had 110 boxes in its store on Monday, and a delivery on Tuesday made the number of boxes 2 times as large. On Wednesday 168 boxes were shipped to a supermarket. Each box left in the store holds 7 packets, every packet holds 4 bars, and every bar snaps into 2 pieces. Kofi, who runs the workshop, keeps more boxes in store than his rival Amara does. How many pieces of chocolate are in the store?

A photographer had 210 photos. They multiplied by 9 times. They added 32 photos. They multiplied by 5 times. They removed 5456 photos (purge). They added 4 photos. 200 photos elsewhere. The time was minutes to hours. How many photos?

In the morning, a concert venue had sold $225 worth of early-bird tickets, even though the venue seats a dozen sections. By midday, seven more identical sales waves pushed the total to eight times its size. In the afternoon, $8 more came in from a walk-up sale. By evening, the venue paid out $1,546 to cover the band's fee. Finally, $31 more trickled in from late online sales. How much revenue did the venue end up with?

A comic book store has 89 back issues of a rare series in stock. A doubling of the stock happens when a second store's inventory is merged in for a joint sale. Then 54 issues are sold during a convention. A distributor deal then multiplies the remaining issues by 9. Finally, a second distributor deal multiplies the stock by 5. How many back issues does the store have now?

A store had 102 products. They removed 57 products from clearance. They added 34 products from new stock. They multiplied by 4 to calculate value. They added 14 more products from returns. There were 12 seasonal items (not counted). How much was the product value?

In the morning the caterers set out 163 chairs in each of the 2 halls of the conference centre. In the afternoon 12 extra chairs were brought from the storeroom and 22 more were borrowed from the cafe. The stage at the front is 10 metres wide. In the evening a late delivery added 3 chairs, and the hotel next door lent 15 more. How many chairs were set out by the end of the evening?

A community garden starts the season with 85 tomato seedlings planted. A spring donation adds 59 more seedlings. A second donation adds 76 more seedlings. The seedlings are then split evenly among 4 garden plots, and only one plot's share is tracked from here. That plot gains 39 more seedlings from a greenhouse, delivered in 60 minutes, or exactly one hour. Finally, 56 more seedlings are added to that plot from a late planting. How many seedlings does that plot have now?

A company began with 140 projects. They multiplied by 9 for revenue scaling. They added 76 projects from new clients. They multiplied by 5 for quarterly planning. They added 55 projects from acquisitions. They subtracted 6107 for consolidation (converting to final projects). Her division managed 12 projects separately. What was the final project count?

A community pantry started the month with 140 tins of soup. A supermarket donated 69 tins, and a church collection brought in 74 more. Every tin holds 5 servings, and the pantry counts its stock in servings rather than in tins. Over the winter 1369 servings were handed out, and half of those went to families with young children. How many servings are left in the pantry?

On Saturday morning a farm split 216 sacks of grain equally between its 2 barns. Later that morning 46 more sacks were delivered to the north barn. Every sack in the north barn holds 8 scoops of grain. In the afternoon 83 scoops were fed to the chickens, and a miller collected 432 scoops. That evening the farmer valued every scoop still in the north barn at 5 pence. How many pence is the north barn's grain worth?
A factory started with 107 units. They removed 93 units. They doubled. They increased 7 times. Finally, 145 units were removed. How many units do they have?

A comic shop began the day with 124 comics on the shelf, while a dozen unopened boxes sat in the back room. Then 2 comics were damaged and pulled from the shelf. A wholesale order removed 103 more comics. A convention order required the remaining stock to grow to 6 times its size. A second expansion made it grow to 5 times its size again. How many comics were needed for that expansion?

A toy company tracked the total number of action figures produced on Line 1, starting with 209 figures. A record shift multiplied the tracked count by 9. A second shift doubled it again. The figures were then split evenly into two shipping batches, and only the first batch's count was tracked. A dozen quality inspectors checked the line that day, though that number has nothing to do with the tracked count. A late addition added 47 more figures to the tracked batch. A bulk order then multiplied the tracked batch by 8. A separate production line, unrelated to this batch, made 600 figures. Finally, a bonus run added 48 more to the tracked batch. How many figures were in the tracked batch?

A café had 50 drinks. They added 8 drinks. They multiplied by 5 times (five batches made). They added 63 drinks. They removed 252 drinks sold. They had a dozen cups available. The inventory at start versus end differed. How many drinks?

Ellis owns more lanterns than his neighbour Rune does. He hung 38 lanterns along the lane and took half of them down when the storm warning came, leaving the rest up. The council then supplied 5 lanterns for every lantern still hanging. A gale destroyed 22 lanterns, and the festival committee donated 71 more. How many lanterns does Ellis have now?

Priya opened a savings account with $182 in it. A holiday bonus from her bank tripled her balance overnight. The next month she paid $166 to cover a family emergency. A matching workplace program then boosted her remaining balance to 8 times its size. She and her brother agreed to split that money in half between their two accounts. Finally, she used $973 of her half to pay off a loan. It had taken her bank 120 minutes, or two hours, to process her very first deposit. How much money, in dollars, did Priya have left after paying off the loan?
